scores.why: Yardstick: the green-on-black with one big halo wash reads as the Matrix, a single note with little variety or typographic voice.
The question typed on the glass of a terminal beside a ruled, grounded desk is a real change in layout and character across every page, with a clear mood and a quiet confidence.
Same desk with a map on the glass; coherent and handsome, but the glass trace is a little busy and the page adds little the parent lacks.
The track diagram's lit rail and tidy cards read as a system and keep the glow, but the Home still looks much like today's, so it is a refinement rather than a new face.
Graphite print with one lit scope is calm and sound but is the most conventional dark dashboard of the field, and the scope is the only character.
A cyanotype drawing sheet with a title block, grid and scalloped bubbles is memorable and totally unlike the Matrix, but the cool grid and heavy caps run a little cold and costumey.
The console with perspective floor, light trails and corner brackets has a real sci-fi identity and lots of variation across the page, close to gimmicky at the edges but disciplined.
Walnut-and-brass card catalogue with a green scope is the most original material story and warm against the green; the brass plates tip toward kitsch, yet it is the most 'oh, that's lovely' mood.
A single lit wire from the glass to the NOW lamp is a genuinely new, meaningful gesture that ties the machine to the list, and the deep-green key calms the page; it vanishes on phone.
Large day numerals with stacked month and weekday give the lists a real typeset rhythm, and the chat hung from a rail is a fresh conversation form, though the offset thread feels slightly awkward.
A larger 48px title with the action at its right end, banding and a cooler ground is tasteful and improves hierarchy, but is subtle and the card shows little of it.
A round week dial is a pleasing idea but is not visible on Home or most pages; the end-mark squares and chevron selects are small refinements on the parent.
Fraunces headings with light figures and small-caps units give the track diagram a typeset voice the owner would enjoy, and the question as the first stop on the rail is lovely.
Small caps and a column of raised keys beside the box add character, but a fourth face and a narrowed box cost more than the gain.
A ruled count strip under the head gives an at-a-glance readout and the lit brand halo restores some phosphor, but it adds little personality to the plain graphite parent.
Section rules with end marks and a lit NOW tick are neat details, but the rail is too quiet at card size and the page is otherwise the parent.
A tiny seven-day trace and a bare foot barely register, and the demo data makes both traces look the same.
Dimension-line ticks and a status line on the input fit the drawing idea nicely but the changes are small and nearly invisible at card scale.
Source Serif titles over mono labels and a status line on the glass make the Blueprint more typeset and give the machine a voice, though serif risks the old fade.
Latched hardware keys for filters and a one-line tube docked at the foot of Chat are fresh, tactile ideas that make the interface feel like real equipment, though the key panel is tall.
A lit wire from Next up to a NOW lamp inside the console is a nice joining line, but short; the lead-word weight is a quiet typographic polish.
Serif sentence-case heads and light figures soften the console elegantly and the NOW tick and vent row add detail, at the cost of some of its machine signature.
Lifting the case and hanging sections from a titled rule is sound typesetting, but the effect barely shows on cards that already used banks.
Big light typed day numerals and bigger drawer titles make the catalogue read by its numbers, a clear typographic step, though thin at small sizes.
A large typewriter figure beside each drawer plate (2 replies, 12 in all) with the unit in brass and a coloured numeral is the most charming new head, and visible on several pages.
Small caps, a steel dot for waiting and the thread opening on 'What's on your mind?' are quiet refinements that read as more typeset, but synthetic caps look light.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the terminal beside the desk and the grounded ruled lists; add one typographic step (numeral days, tracked small caps) so the desk is as designed as the glass.
Keep the lit wire and the deep-green key; shorten the run on To do so it does not read as a glowing border, and give the phone a short stub at the NOW row so the idea survives on one column.
Keep the large day numerals; restore the Status signal legend, and rebalance the chat rail so Vera's replies are not squeezed to half the thread.
Keep the latched keys and the docked one-line tube; make the key panel compact (two rows) so Ideas is not pushed down, and keep a visible Send-where-I-am label.
Keep the typed drawer count with brass unit and pencil line; take the numeral larger (4rem+) and bring the same figure onto Home so the idea reaches the page people open first.
Keep the Fraunces heads and small-caps units; run the same pairing on figures and section heads throughout and make the trace carry real data so it is not a lone spike.
Keep the walnut-and-brass material story; cool the brass plates and cut the stamped ornament a step so it reads crafted rather than kitsch.

judges.notes: The carried desk terminal family leads: the question typed on a case's glass with a grounded desk beside it is a distinct identity and shows on every page. Among newcomers, ideas that add meaning beat ones that add trim: the lit wire joining the glass to the next thing due, the large typed figure beside a drawer plate, hardware-like latched keys, and typeset pairing with serif heads and small caps. Many r14 mutants are one-change steps on a parent whose effect the cards barely show (traces, end marks, raster, rounded corners); those score near their parents. The weakest changes are tiny sparklines and a quiet rail that disappear at half size. Note that Fraunces and Source Serif only help where the whole page takes the pairing. The Signal Catalogue is the boldest material and the warmest, worth developing if the brass is cooled.

parts.what: Fraunces titles and section heads, light lining figures, small-caps units
slightly cooler ground with warmer bone neutral words; walnut and brass plate material as runner
large typed count figure beside the plate with brass unit and a pencilled line; or 48px title with the page's one action at the right end
section rule closing in a small solid end mark in the section's colour; or sections hung from a single titled rule
terminal case with the question typed on the glass and status line below; bezel lip and vent row as runner
terminal foot cut to lamp, state and Status link; title block cut to lamp and name

scores.why: Clear Vera box and bright send key, but 42 of 55 Home targets are under 44px, the glow is the same everywhere, and nothing but green separates the kinds of thing.

The question is typed inside the tube, then From, mic and a bright Send, then ways to start, so the first glance on the phone reads tube, box, action; there are no small targets, and the steel here-tab and lamp status line work as one system.
Same sound desk as Joined, with a scatter map in the glass and a plain separate composer; the eye goes title, Send, content, and the thumb gets 0 of 62 small targets.

One calm panel holds the bold question with its lit key word, the composer and a bright Send, and it has only 1 small target; it is clear and usable, but it is close to today's page across the content.
Calm graphite page with a lit scope and 0 small targets; it works, but the scope title and the date are small and the page changes little from today beyond the ground.
Uppercase labels and dashed chips give the tabs, fields and selects one drafting grammar, but 16 targets are under 44px and the page is denser and more all-caps than a phone at night wants.
Full-width ways-to-start rows are good thumb targets and the SEND key is clear, but 20 small targets remain, the caps are heavy, and the stacked rows push the monitor down.
The walnut and brass ground is a real change and its lamps are legible, but the tab bar is a row of heavy cells, the type is mixed, and 7 targets are small.
The wire adds nothing on the phone, the question shrinks to tiny small caps in the tube, and the dim deep-green Send weakens the one action the owner wants kept bright.
The day numeral and the rail-hung chat are good ideas for scanning, but neither shows on the Home card, and cutting the foot's facts and the Status legend loses information.

The title a step larger with the page's one action at its right end tells the family where to look and what to do, and the alternate-row band keeps the eye on a facts column; the cost is a double add affordance.
Selects drawn as buttons with a flipping chevron are a clear control, but the week dial repeats what the list says and squeezes the month grid to wrapped three-line titles.
The Fraunces pairing and the seven-day trace cannot be seen on the Home card, and with one day of data the trace says nothing, so the page reads as the parent.
True small caps and a column of keys beside the box could help scanning, but a fourth face is added and the narrower box makes its footer wrap.

A ruled strip of Today, Plans, To do and Late counts, each a link, answers 'what is overdue' at a glance, and lighting the brand and here-tab brings back the tube's halo, but it drops the steel here-block.
A NOW tick on a rail and checkboxes drawn as lit squares are tidy signals, but they sit below the fold and a 2px tick is hard to see at a phone's size.
A scanline band lies across the NEXT UP title inside the glass on its Home card, so the headline is hidden; the 72px trace is quiet and the radius change is cosmetic.
The lamp line 'Ready, nothing waiting on Vera' under the question is a useful state signal for the family, but it sits on the dense Blueprint grid with 16 small targets.
A status line on the glass ('4 plans, 3 late, Vera is listening') gives the Home glance a readout, but it carries the Blueprint's density and 17 small targets.
Latched filter keys with lamps are a clear on/off control and the docked chat tube is a good idea, but the filter panel is taller and the Home card looks like the parent.
The wire is short and the smaller question with a block cursor is a quiet gain, but the page is the Grid Console with its 20 small targets.
The Fraunces pairing and the NOW tick are barely visible on the card, and the vent row is too fine to read, so the page is the parent with a fourth face.
Hanging sections from a titled rule and holding text to one measure is a sound typographic rule, but the cards cannot show it and the Grid Console's 20 small targets stay.
A large light day numeral beside month and weekday is good for scanning dates, but the numeral is thin on the dark card and Home never shows it.
A typed drawer count leading each page tells you at a glance what the page holds, but it only wraps on a phone, and its tally figure is moderate in size.
A steel dot for waiting in place of a red ring for off is a calmer, more honest signal, and small caps help typesetting, but the synthetic small caps read thin.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the larger title with the one action at the head's right end, and drop the duplicate add summary below it so a page has one add affordance. Keep the faint band, but add a hairline rule so it still works with only two or three rows.

Keep the typed question with the composer inside the tube, so box and action are one thing on the first screen. Add a count or lamp strip under it so Home answers what is late as well as what is next.
Keep the count strip, and give the Late cell a grounded warm tone so it separates from the others. Keep the steel reverse block for the here-tab and put the halo on the brand and mark only.
Keep the readout line on the glass, and lift it onto the Desk Terminal, where targets are already large. Drop the serif titles for sans, and keep the mono for the line.
Keep the day numeral and the rail-hung chat, but keep the signal legend on Status. Make the numeral weight 400 so it holds on the dark ground.
Keep the wire as a two-column idea, and give the phone a short stub to the NOW lamp. Restore the bright Send key, and keep the question at its full size inside the tube.
Fix the scanline band that covers the NEXT UP title before anything else. The trace idea is worth keeping only if it reaches Home's counts.

judges.notes: The Desk Terminal family leads on use: the tube states the question and the next thing due, a bright Send follows, and the targets are all at least 44px, where today's page has 42 of 55 below. This round's one-change steps mostly cannot be seen on the phone Home card (the wire, the trace, small caps, the band), and the demo's Home is the setup page. So I scored what the cards and the notes support, and gave most weight to the changes that help the first glance: r14-mut-3's head and action, r14-mut-7's count strip and r14-mut-11's readout on the glass. The Blueprint, Grid and Signal families are bolder in look, but they bring 16 to 20 small targets and heavier all-caps. r14-mut-9 shows a visible glitch on the glass. The owner's test, change across the content, favours the Desk family, which has a steel case, a graphite ground and a typed tube, over the Track and Long Persistence mutants that sit very near today.

parts.what: Select drawn as a raised button with a chevron that flips open; a clean list; bright Send key
Phone tab bar with a steel reverse block marking the here-tab, large icons and labels
One mono lamp line saying what Vera is doing ('Ready, nothing waiting on Vera'); a steel dot for waiting in place of red
One panel: bold question with a lit key word, composer, From, mic, bright Send, then outlined ways to start

scores.why: Today's page: the glow DNA is intact, but it is the all-green, too-bright, too-contrasty monochrome the owner started by asking to calm.

Grounded steel slate, a lit tube with a typed question, a Coming up track with a NOW dot and a chat hung from a rail: the owner's line language, the glow where the phosphor is, and changes across every page.
Same desk with the radar turned into a plans bar chart and a map on Ideas; good content-level change, but the machine panel feels a little busier for little gain.
Track Diagram: Signal Box's subway rails carried through To do, Coming up, Lately added and chat, with a glowing hero; strongly on the owner's favourite, though several tracks make it busy.
Graphite print with one lit instrument, calm and grounded but plainer, with little line art and a flatter feel than the leaders.
Cyanotype blueprint grid with a title block and wavy bubbles is a real change, but the ruled sheet leans away from the CRT soul and the drafting conceit is loud.
Control panel with light trails that delimit areas and lead the eye, perspective floor and the lowest green share; a rich, line-led design, though a bit heavy and the chat looks plain.
Walnut and brass card catalogue: the brown frames and tan plates are exactly the warm materials the owner said clash with the CRT motif, whatever the craft.

Desk Terminal plus one lit wire from the glass to the NOW lamp is the owner's kind of line that draws the eye through the frame; the deep-green key is a risk to the primary button's glow but the rest holds.

Large day numerals on the Coming up track are a visible improvement to the list the owner admires, and the chat rail is on-style; the centred spine squeezes Vera's replies and dropping the foot facts is a small loss.
Bigger page titles with the action at the head's end and banded rows reach every page and add a typeset feel, but the cooler ground and faint bands are subtle on the cards.
The week dial is a charming glanceable figure but only on Plans and it repeats the list; the rule end marks and chevron selects are small refinements.

Fraunces headings with light figures and small-cap units, and a chat that opens on the question as the first stop on the track, change the typography across every page while keeping the rails and glow.
True small caps are a good typographic touch but the ways-to-start column squeezes the Home box and adds a fourth face.
The haloed brand and current tab bring back some tube light, and the count strip adds a glanceable readout, but it sits on the plainer graphite parent and loses the reverse-video here marker.
Rules with end marks and a NOW tick are tasteful line work but nearly invisible at card size, and the base is a plainer design.
A seven-day trace and squarer corners are faint, quiet changes; the page barely differs from its parent.
Dimension-line ticks and a status line on the input are neat, but the raster is barely perceptible and the blueprint base still drifts from the CRT.
The status line on the glass is a lovely idea and the serif headings are visible, but the blueprint ruled-sheet frame still dominates and the 12px mono labels shrink.
Latched keys with lit lamps for filters and a one-line tube docked at the foot of Chat are tangible, characterful controls; the key panel grows tall and the tube is cramped.

Grid Console with a real phosphor wire from the tube to the lit NOW: light trails that lead the eye through the frame, most varied colour with the least neon, and the glass question's blinking cursor.
The Grid Console with Folio's serif pairing and a white-hot NOW tick is typeset and handsome, but it loses the console's tracked-caps machine voice and brings a fourth face.
Lighter case and unboxed rule heads are tasteful, but the changes are subtle on pages that already use banks.
Large day numerals are nice in the catalogue, but it is still the brown-and-brass room the owner finds off-motif.
A tally figure on each head is a good readout, but again on walnut and brass plates that fight the green.
Small caps and a quieter steel dot help, and the thread opening on the question is a nice touch, but the brown catalogue remains.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the wire from the tube to NOW and the small-cap labels; keep the Send key bright phosphor green (the owner wants the primary button lit) and shorten the wire on To do so it does not read as a glowing border.
Keep as the bar: the track, the NOW dot and the chat rail are right. Add a visible content change, such as the large day numerals from r14-mut-2, so the family sees more than the corner.
Keep the serif heads, light figures and the thread that opens on the question. Check that the Fraunces face stays calm beside two others, and make the trace show real variety.
Keep the large day numerals; give the chat rail back its width (left-aligned spine, not centred) and restore the foot's status facts or move them into the Status legend.
Keep the lit wire and the cursor that blinks only while focused; carry the same wire to the To do list and keep Coming up first on Home, with the console's tracked caps untouched.
Keep the latched keys with lamps, but shrink the key panel so Ideas is not pushed down, and give the docked tube more width by moving From and the location tick into a second line.
Keep the status line on the glass, as it lifts straight into any design; do not carry the 12px mono labels.
The chat's typed-index rhythm and Day numerals work, but swap the walnut and brass for slate and steel before it can win.

judges.notes: Judged on the owner's own tests: lines that delimit and lead the eye (Signal Box's rails, now the Desk Terminal's track and the Grid Console's trails), the glow kept where the phosphor is, grounded steel-slate colour elsewhere, and visible change on content across pages. The Desk Terminal family and the Track Diagram family carry that best, and the one lit wire from the glass to the NOW is the best new idea because it is a line that means something. Brown and brass (Signal Catalogue) is penalised, as the owner said warm browns fight the CRT. The blueprint reads as a different theme rather than a refined Phosphor. Serif and tallied-figure changes help typesetting but only count where they are seen on the pages. Simplicity breaks ties in favour of the plainer variant, so the parents stay close to their children's scores.

parts.what: Terminal case with the question typed on the glass and a block cursor; add a one-line status on the glass
Coming up track: NOW dot, large mono day numeral with month over weekday, time and in-N-days columns
Thread hung on a rail that opens on What's on your mind? as its first stop, with Vera's lines on nodes
Green-black glass, steel-slate case and thin lines in amber and violet, with the least neon in the field
Fraunces heads with light lining figures and small-cap units; a larger page title with the action at its end
Layered halo on the bar's mark, wordmark and current tab; phosphor wire and light trails

scores.why: Yardstick: real lit glass, radar and halo, but one wash of glow on a black page, little structure, and the Matrix look the family named.
The question typed in lit VT323 on the glass with a halo cursor, the full-gauge Status tube and the case on every page make the tube the page's soul, while the ground and the rest are calm.
Joined plus a real radar map with numbered halo blips and a trace chart on the glass; richer light, same calm elsewhere.
Tasteful track-line structure but the glass is the same as today's and the tube is only on Home, so the tube's soul reads as little changed.
Graphite print with a strong scope tube on Home; the rest of the page is nearly plain, with light staying in one place.
Cyanotype grid with tiles and a real bezelled tube; distinctive but the page body is a drawing sheet and the glow is held far back.
Phosphor trails, grid floor in the monitor and a lit Send key keep the tube alive on a console frame; uppercase Archivo light titles are a fresh voice.
Walnut and brass with a green ECG scope is a fresh material idea and the glass stays strong, but brass plates pull the soul toward steampunk.
Keeps the Desk Terminal glass, but the typed question shrinks to a tiny small-cap line and loses the big lit sentence; the wire is a lovely idea that no card shows.
Same glowing desk as Mapped with the foot trimmed and a rail in the chat; adds structure without touching the light.
Mapped with a cooler ground and a banded list; the glass is untouched and the band is a small gain across list pages.
Week dial is a nice figure but sits on Plans only; the glass and Home match the parent.
Fraunces titles on the track diagram give a typeset voice, but a serif is cooler to the CRT soul and the tube is unchanged.
Small caps and a wheat shift are barely visible against the parent; a quiet gain.
Brings the layered halo back to the mark, wordmark and current tab, which is directly what the owner asked, and the tally strip is useful; the page is otherwise Long Persistence.
Section rules with end marks and a NOW tick are tidy but off the tube; the soul is no different from the parent.
Traces and squarer corners are small and quiet; no extra phosphor.
Faint raster and wider bloom on the glass plus a status line on the input add life to the Blueprint, but the effect is hard to see.
A status line on the glass ending in 'Vera is listening' is the one idea that makes the tube speak; the serif titles pull a little from the CRT feel.
Latched filter keys and a docked one-line tube are tactile and aim at the soul, but the cards show only a lit cursor in the bar.
The wire from the tube to NOW and a blinking cursor in the question are the right instincts for a lit page; the cards show only a stub.
Fraunces and a vented bezel give a more crafted tube, though the serif on a console cools it.
Lighter case round deeper glass is a good small material step; the rest is the parent.
Day numerals and a bigger drawer label help reading; the catalogue's brass remains the main character.
A typed drawer count beside the brass plate and a wider bloom with raster on the glass: the one change that puts a lit figure at the head of every page.
Small caps and a steel waiting dot are calm refinements; the glass and plates are as before.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the big lit typed question with its halo cursor and the dial on Status; add the layered halo to the bar's mark and wordmark and to the here tab, as in r14-mut-7, so the page frame shares the tube's light.
Keep the radar map and trace chart. Add a status line on the glass (r14-mut-11) and the lit wire to NOW, so the tube visibly connects to the list.
Keep the wire, but restore the question to its larger lit size; the tiny small-cap question is the one loss. Show the wire on a card so judges can see it.
Lift the glass status line ('4 plans, 3 late, Vera is listening') into the Desk Terminal's tube; keep the heads in a sans so the serif does not cool the CRT.
Take the halo on mark, wordmark and here tab onto Desk Terminal and keep the steel-reverse here block as well, so the 'where I am' signal is not lost.
The lit drawer count is the head idea worth lifting; put its figure in phosphor with a halo, and pair it with the glass bloom and raster.

judges.notes: The Desk Terminal family clearly has the most soul. The sentence is typed on a real tube with a halo and block cursor, the page frame is calm, and the case recurs on Home, Ideas and Status. Joined, Mapped, Railed and Banded are nearly identical on my cards and differ in small page-level changes, so they rank by how much they add outside the tube. Mapped's radar map and trace and Joined's dial are the best light-bearing figures. The weaker parts are the three Long Persistence and Track Diagram variants, whose changes sit in corners or in tabs, and the Blueprint, whose light is hidden under the grid. The two promising ideas are the lit wire from the glass to NOW, and the status line on the glass: both make the light mean something. The halo returning to the mark and tab is the cheapest way to answer the owner's request for the original effect, and should be folded into whichever design wins.

parts.what: Typed question in lit VT323 with halo and block cursor on a scanlined tube, glow limited to the glass
Cased tube with Vera's header, typed question, Next up and a radar map or trace; plus a status line on the glass
Page title plate with a large typed count and unit beside it
Dot rows showing 3 of 4 on, with a lit lamp at the case's foot; a steel dot for waiting
Status gauge on the glass with tick scale, lit needle and a big mono readout; or an ECG scope trace

scores.why: Yardstick: green on black with little but green, flat card grid, nothing structural; the Matrix read the family complained about.
Cased terminal beside the page, steel plates and bone ink give real material change on every page; Status sidebar is dense and the terminal repeats on every page.
Same desk with a mapped lamp index; more informative but slightly busier, and the grey-blue ground borders on a tinted wash.
Track diagram with dated rail on To do and lit track on Status is a real structural idea; condensed heavy titles feel loud and the Status sheet is mostly the old card grid.
Graphite print page with one lit scope is calm and the To do scope reflects content, but the Plans and Settings pages are bland tables and the colour is almost all grey.
Blueprint sheets with title blocks and grid change the whole page's grammar, but the teal-black is nearly monochrome and the grid reads as an editor or CAD theme.
Square-cell console with trailing light rails, wide-tracked titles and a live Plans grid is the most distinct page structure on the sheet; the wide caps title borders on costume.
Walnut-and-brass wash is the muddy bronze the owner warned against; the label plates are a costume and the green is reduced to a few tubes.
Primary key grounded and the lit wire joining terminal to NOW is a content-level link on To do, though it reads as a glowing border and vanishes on phones.
Day numerals and rail chat are invisible on these cards and cutting the legend loses the shape code; practically the parent.
Larger 48px titles with the bright primary key at the head's right and banded rows show on every page and bring the phosphor back as a lit action; double add affordance on To do is a flaw.
Week dial on Plans and rule end marks are content-relevant, but the dial squeezes the month grid and repeats information, and Status and Settings are unchanged.
Fraunces titles and light figures change the typographic voice on every page, which the owner values; the trace spike is meaningless in demo data and serif titles are a familiar fade.
Small caps and a wheat shift are too subtle to see at card size; near-duplicate of the parent with a fourth font.
Count strip links across pages is content-level and the lit wordmark returns some tube light, but the graphite base stays bland and the here-tab code is lost.
Rule end marks and NOW tick are 1px quiet and unseen at half size; near-duplicate of its parent.
Seven-day traces too small to see and show the same spike; squarer corners barely register; the weakest justification on the sheet.
Oblique end ticks on rules are barely visible and look like stray marks; blueprint parent otherwise unchanged.
Serif titles with mono labels and end marks visibly retype the whole Blueprint and calm its shouting caps; small mono labels and a faded serif risk remain.
Latched filter keys are a good hardware control on To do, but that is the only visible change, and the key panel gets taller.
Grid Console with a lit wire and lead-word medium rows; the wire is short and the row weight change is subtle at this size.
Serif heads and light figures soften the console's shouting caps on every page, and the NOW tick with time inside the To do list is a real content-level signal; four faces is its cost.
Lighter bezel and rule heads are subtle and the page already used trails; near-duplicate of Grid Console.
Big day numerals help To do's cards but the bronze wash and costume plates remain, and the numerals appear on one page only.
Drawer counts beside each title add a glanceable figure on every page, but the label plates and brown ground are still the bronze costume.
Small caps and steel dots quieten Status but leave the walnut wash and plate costume untouched.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the serif heads, light figures and the NOW tick with time; drop the vent row, which is invisible, and cut to three faces by letting Martian Mono do VT323's job outside the glass.
Keep the 48px title with the lit primary key at the right but remove the duplicate Add fold below it; give the bands a touch more contrast so they show on To do.
Keep the wire and the deep-green key but shorten the run so it does not read as a border on the terminal, and give phones a short stub into the NOW row.
Keep the rail-and-bank structure and square cells; set the page title in a lighter, less tracked weight so it stops shouting and let the phosphor halo sit on the one live bank only.
The count strip is the right kind of content-level change; restore the steel-reverse here marker for the current tab and widen the strip's figures so cells are not mostly arrows.
The dial earns its place only if smaller and placed so the month grid keeps its width; consider moving it into the head strip and extend the lit track on Status to Keys and Connected to.
Keep serif titles with mono labels but raise the mono labels back to 13px and keep the end mark; it is the cleanest typographic upgrade on the Blueprint.

judges.notes: Most of the field is a one-change step on a carried parent and still looks like its parent at half size; I scored those low where the change cannot be seen on any card (traces, end ticks, rail chat, vents, bezel tokens). The three Signal Catalogue entries share a bronze wash and plate costume the owner warned against, and their small edits cannot fix that. The Blueprint family changes the page's whole grammar but stays near-monochrome teal and risks an editor or CAD look. The best new moves change the type voice or put a lit signal inside list content (serif Grid Console with its NOW tick, the lit primary key at the head, the wire to NOW, the count strip). Light is the weakest area: few designs return the original layered halo to words and marks, and only the primary key and glass do it with spark.

parts.what: dated rail with stamps at each row and a lit now node; or faint steel banding on alternate rows
due scope on To do (late spikes, now line, week divisions); or the round week dial with today lit
section head as a titled rule with a trailing light rail; or a small solid end block closing each rule
one lit wire from the terminal into the NOW row; or a white-hot NOW tick with the time beside it
filters as latched keys with a lamp on the one that is down; or the cased terminal's segmented view and month keys
larger title with the page's one lit primary action at the right end; or a ruled strip of linked counts under the head
